children.text: From a blank page to a generated PDF: a complete tour of Imprime in 5 steps.
Five steps to go from an empty template to an automatically generated PDF.
Pick a format: A4 portrait, A4 landscape or 16:9.
Place text, shapes, images and groups on each page.
Whatever changes from one PDF to the next becomes a variable.
Show a block on a condition, repeat it for every line.
Send the values, get a PDF ready to share.
It all starts on the My Templates screen of your account.
Pick a page format: A4 portrait, A4 landscape or 16:9.
from its card to start designing.
the format is set once, when you create the template.
Each page is a canvas: shapes stack from back to front.
Each shape keeps its own x / y position.
Laid out in a row, with an even gap.
Laid out in a column: ideal for lists.
Layered on top of each other, aligned together.
Anything that changes from one PDF to the next becomes a variable, referenced by name.
Name, amount, date… with an optional max length.
True or false: drives the IF of a block.
A logo or photo specific to each PDF.
Quote lines, attendees…: drives the FOR.
One template adapts to every case: optional blocks and lists of any length.
Show a block on a condition
A shape, or a whole page, only appears in the PDF when a boolean is true. Negate it to get the opposite.
A group is drawn once per list item. In a vertical group set to hug, copies stack and push the rest down.
Send one value per variable, by name: Imprime renders the PDF.
Export warnings flag anything that doesn't fit on the page.
What saves you from surprises at export time.
Size boxes for the longest value
Text wraps but isn't measured: give each box room for its longest possible value.
Set a max length: a value that's too long fails the export instead of silently overflowing.
Nothing flows to the next page
A shape that starts below the page bottom is left out of the PDF: cap your lists.
With no value, a boolean hides its block either way. A default avoids the surprise.
Then reuse the same template for every client.
